text:
Predicates:
TwinOrTriplet(x) ::: x is a twin or triplet.
SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings.
SameAgeSiblings(x) ::: x has siblings who are the same age.
ComplainsOftenAboutSiblings(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
DevelopsStrongBonds(x) ::: x develops strong bonds with family members.
Premises:
∀x (TwinOrTriplet(x) → SpendTimeWithSiblings(x)) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time with siblings.
∀x (SameAgeSiblings(x) → TwinOrTriplet(x)) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (ComplainsOftenAboutSiblings(x) → SameAgeSiblings(x)) ::: If people complain often about siblings, then their siblings are the same age.
∀x (¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) → ¬DevelopsStrongBonds(x)) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds.
∀x (SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) → ¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time with siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
( (TwinOrTriplet(luke) ∧ DevelopsStrongBonds(luke)) ∨ (¬TwinOrTriplet(luke) ∧ ¬DevelopsStrongBonds(luke)) ) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds, or neither.
